sources.title: Claude Gay (Q1096785), verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-11-05): English label 'Claude Gay', description 'French botanist, naturalist and illustrator (1800-1873)', Spanish label 'Claudio Gay', no Korean label, born 18 March 1800, died 29 November 1873, citizenship France and Chile. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Memoria Chilena (National Library of Chile), 'Claudio Gay Mouret (1800-1873)', read in full (Spanish). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: dated outline of his life (arrival in Chile on 8 December 1828, teaching at the Colegio de Santiago, the 1830 contract to explore and study the territory, about twelve years of travel from Atacama to Chiloe plus Peru in 1839, the collection that became the Gabinete de Historia Natural in 1836, Chilean citizenship by grace in December 1841, the Historia fisica y politica de Chile of 1844-1871 in about thirty volumes with an atlas and an eight-volume history, his last visit in 1863, death in 1873). A celebratory national-library page; its description of the Lastarria-Bello debate gives no substance.

Memoria Chilena, 'Contrato con el Gobierno de Chile' (Gay minisite), read in full (Spanish): the 1830 contract with the minister Diego Portales to travel from the Atacama desert to Chiloe studying geography, geology, botany and zoology, to deliver a general natural history with plates, a geography, a geology and statistics after four years, to set up a Gabinete de Historia Natural and to place his library at the project's service, against a monthly payment, instruments, official support and a prize of 3,000 pesos; and the note that the work took nearly forty years instead of four. The page gives 25 pesos a month where other sources give 125, and no account of obstacles.

Memoria Chilena, 'Historia fisica y politica de Chile (1844-1871)' (Gay minisite), read in full (Spanish): how Minister Mariano Egaña commissioned a Chilean history in 1839 and financed a trip to Lima for documents, Gay's method of gathering documents and oral accounts (about fifteen manuscripts, interviews with participants in independence) with advice from Andres Bello, the structure of the work (sixteen natural-history volumes, two on agriculture, eight of history and two documentary volumes), and the 1844 Lastarria-Bello polemic in which Bello held up Gay's work as the model of documented history. It relies on secondary studies and is favourable to Gay and Bello.

Universidad de Chile, 'Claudio Gay Mouret' (page on its illustrious figures), read (Spanish): a short summary of his studies, the three-year agreement with the government, his founding of the natural history museum, the 1839 history proposal, citizenship by grace in 1841, membership of the university in 1843 and the 1844-1871 publication. It prints an impossible year (1956) for a French academy membership and gives three years where other sources say four for the contract, so it is used only as a cross-check.

Carlos Ossenbach, 'Orchids of the Southern Cone (1830-2000), Part I: Claude Gay's Physical and political history of Chile', Lankesteriana 22(3), 2022, pages 181-206 (English), downloaded as a PDF and read in full for the biographical section (the orchid taxonomy was not assessed): his training and recruitment, the 1830 contract terms, expeditions 1830-1841, the 1832 return to France to buy instruments and books, the botanical collaborators in Paris, financing difficulties, the 1863 visit and pension, and criticism: Carl Reiche (1910) called the orchid treatment one of the weakest collaborations, which Ossenbach rejects as unjustifiable given how little was known, and Gay himself wrote that about half of the orchid species were poorly known. A botanical-history paper in tribute; some of its biographical points are drawn from Chilean secondary literature.

Melica Munoz Schick, '100 anos de la Seccion Botanica del Museo Nacional de Historia Natural (1889-1989)', Boletin del Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de Chile 42 (1991), pages 181-202 (Spanish), downloaded as a PDF and read in full (the Gay section is the opening page): the 14 September 1830 contract, his travels between Copiapo and Chiloe, the museum he had installed in 1838 in a room on calle Catedral, the collections taken to France and studied by his collaborators (Barneoud, Clos, Naudin, Remy, Richard, Desvaux, Montagne), the 28 volumes and 2 atlases published in Paris from 1845, the 1,500 duplicate specimens kept in Santiago as isotypes, and the rise of the known Chilean flora from about 300 to 3,767 species. Written by a museum botanist; independent of the Memoria Chilena pages.

persistence.rationale: [src_gay_memoria_bio, src_gay_memoria_contract, src_gay_ossenbach, src_gay_munoz | 1830-1871 | national-library pages, botanical-history paper, museum botanist's history] Four independent descriptions agree on a sustained programme: about twelve years of expeditions from Atacama to Chiloe until all provinces were explored in 1841 (Memoria Chilena, Ossenbach), followed by about 27 years of publication of some thirty volumes between 1844 and 1871 (Ossenbach, Munoz Schick), through difficulties in financing (Ossenbach), on a project the contract had planned for four years and Memoria Chilena says took nearly forty. The delay is attributed to resources and personal circumstances (the latter not used here), so the row scores the documented continuity of effort and not speed.

curiosity.rationale: [src_gay_ossenbach, src_gay_memoria_bio, src_gay_memoria_work | 1821-1844 | botanical-history paper, national-library pages] He turned from medicine and pharmacy to botany and entomology in Paris, then taught himself physics, chemistry, geology and comparative anatomy (Ossenbach, citing a Chilean biographer), travelled with the botanist Balbis in 1822 (Memoria Chilena), and went on to cover botany, zoology, geology, geography and, from 1839, history in one project. The breadth is documented, but much of its scope was set by the government contract, and the self-teaching claim reaches us through a secondary source. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): lowered from 70/0.55 to 66/0.48 because the breadth was largely prescribed by the 1830 contract and the self-study evidence is second-hand.

proactive_agency.rationale: [src_gay_ossenbach, src_gay_memoria_bio, src_gay_memoria_work | 1828-1863 | botanical-history paper, national-library pages] He accepted an offer to go to a country he describes as unknown to naturalists (Ossenbach quoting his journal), sailed to France in 1832 to buy instruments and books and to seek funds, although Memoria Chilena says the request to the French government was rejected, went to Lima in 1839 for historical documents (Memoria Chilena, Ossenbach) and returned to Chile in 1863 to publish in Spanish and hand over his library and collections (Memoria Chilena). These are self-directed steps documented by two independent writers; the motives are partly Gay's own words in a secondary quotation.

collaboration.rationale: [src_gay_munoz, src_gay_ossenbach | 1842-1871 | museum botanist's history, botanical-history paper] Both sources independently list the Paris specialists who described his collections (Richard for the orchids, Montagne for cryptogams, Barneoud, Clos, Naudin, Remy, Desvaux), and Ossenbach adds that he wrote the treatment of 103 families himself and had early mentors in Jussieu and Richard; Memoria Chilena says Bello advised his historical method. The behaviour, organising outside specialists around his own collections, is documented; there is no source on how he worked with them day to day, so the trait inference is moderate. Limit: Reiche's criticism of one collaboration (the orchids) shows the quality was uneven.

analytical_rigor.rationale: [src_gay_memoria_work, src_gay_ossenbach | 1839-1849 | national-library page, botanical-history paper] Memoria Chilena says he gathered about fifteen manuscripts and interviewed participants in the independence period, applied natural-science methods with Bello's advice, and was held up by Bello as the model of documented history against Lastarria's speculative approach; Ossenbach reports that his own text calls about half of the orchid species poorly known, and that only 21 of 49 orchid names remain accepted. The favourable framing comes from sources that follow Bello's side of the 1844 debate and no independent assessment of his historical method was found, so the row stays low in confidence.

(3) Engraving reproduction, Memoria Chilena item MC0005523 (AF0010251): item-level 'patrimonio cultural comun' but creator and date unidentified (reproduction made by the University of Chile photographic department), so a US public-domain basis cannot be stated. Alternatives checked (one bounded retry): BND/Memoria Chilena Franceschi photograph (no item licence, footer 'Algunos derechos reservados'), Memoria Chilena engraving MC0005523 ('patrimonio cultural comun' but no creator or date), Commons Laemlein 1845 (source PDF unreachable).
